thread:
maya: FYI starting apac-edge4 cluster bring-up now. nodegroup create is failing with mixed errors: quota, spot interruptions, and a few AMI kernel panics. rolling status in #infra-runbooks.
jon: ok seeing the same. `ec2:InsufficientInstanceCapacity` then `InstanceLaunchLifecycleError` for some h100 spot requests.
ravi: any pricing alerts? spot price spike can cause immediate termination of launch attempts.
maya: yeah spot price spiked in apac-edge4 around 12:02 UTC. autoscaler tried 6x requests, 4 failed. fallback to on-demand was triggered but somehow the launch template used the new ami `redwood-gpu-ami-v3.2` which hasn't been validated with driver 525.85 yet.
sophia: that AMI was built yesterday for eu-west tests. we didn't promote it to apac. looks like a variable in the launch-template override got set to latest instead of pinned.
maya: deploy-bot: record rollout step and annotate root cause?
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] recorded: rollout/edge4 -> failed nodegroup creates (spot capacity + unvalidated AMI). ticket #INC-8732 created.
jon: logs show kubelet OOM/kernel panic on 3 nodes that did get provisioned. kernel message: "NVRM: GPU panic" then systemd-reboot.
ravi: likely driver mismatch. on-demand instances that succeeded are on ami v3.2 (driver 525.60), but our node image expects 525.85. that explains the panics.
maya: action plan: 1) pause further autoscaler retries 2) pin launch-template to v3.1 AMI 3) drain and cordon affected nodes 4) roll back AMI promotion pipeline.
sophia: I can patch the TF var to pin AMI and re-run plan+apply. who can hold the autoscaler?
jon: i'll scale-down the cluster autoscaler and set max nodes to current count to prevent new launches. `kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy cluster-autoscaler --replicas=0`.
maya: doing node cordon/drain in parallel. `kubectl cordon gpu-edge-14` then `kubectl drain gpu-edge-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
sophia: TF patch ready, pushing now. note: need to also update ASG lifecycle hook timeout for on-demand fallback - previously short and causing launch timeouts.
ravi: also double-check ENI quotas. I saw `ENI limit exceeded` on 2 failed launches before the spot error. sounds like subnet IP exhaustion in that availability zone.
maya: opened cloud quota request but that's slow. short-term: move more nodegroups across AZs, reduce per-node ENI usage by using smaller pods or increase secondary IP pool if possible.
jon: after scaling autoscaler to 0, one more node attempted and failed with `eni limit exceeded`. patched launch-template to pin ami v3.1 and changed subnets to include az-b.
sophia: apply finished; waiting for ASG to launch new nodes on v3.1.
maya: new nodes coming up on v3.1. initial health checks passing. kubelet stable.
ravi: monitoring for GPU driver panics. so far none. SLO for bring-up latency extended by ~22m.
sophia: on the AMI pipeline side, adding extra validation: GPU driver matrix test + kubelet + nvidia-smi smoke. gating promotion to other regions.
maya: we'll also add a small preflight that checks spot price history and ENI headroom before opening mass node requests. link to runbook: https://intranet.redwood/infra/runbooks/edge-provision
jon: re-enable cluster-autoscaler when 3 nodes healthy. i'll do it in 5m.
maya: thanks. summary: root cause = combination of spot price spike -> fallback + unpinned AMI (driver mismatch) + subnet ENI headroom不足. mitigations: pin AMI, patch TF, spread AZs, add AMI validation and preflight checks. follow-up: add alert for AMI-promote without validation and an autoscaler safety gate.
srebot: [srebot] incident logged: INC-8732, priority P2. runbook assigned to maya/sophia/ravi.
maya: closing thread once full health green. ping me if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
